definitions.gloss: to set free, to release, to liberate
definitions.explanation: To physically release something from confinement, such as freeing an animal from a cage or untying something that was bound.

definitions.gloss: to unleash, to free from constraints
definitions.explanation: To figuratively release something from restriction, such as freeing oneself from stress, obligations, or oppression.

examples.japanese: {鳥|とり}を{空|そら}に{解|と}き{放|はな}った。
examples.english: I released the bird into the sky.

examples.japanese: {鎖|くさり}を{外|はず}して{犬|いぬ}を{解|と}き{放|はな}った。
examples.english: I removed the chain and set the dog free.

examples.japanese: {捕|と}らえた{魚|さかな}を{川|かわ}に{解|と}き{放|はな}つことにした。
examples.english: I decided to release the caught fish back into the river.

examples.japanese: ストレスから{解|と}き{放|はな}たれたい。
examples.english: I want to be freed from stress.

examples.japanese: {旅|たび}に{出|で}て{日常|にちじょう}から{解|と}き{放|はな}たれた。
examples.english: I went on a trip and was freed from daily routine.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{束縛|そくばく}から{解|と}き{放|はな}たれ、{自由|じゆう}を{手|て}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: Freed from years of constraint, I obtained my freedom.

notes:
USAGE:
{解|と}き{放|はな}つ is a compound verb from {解|と}く (to untie) + {放|はな}つ (to release). It is a godan verb conjugating as {解|と}き{放|はな}たない, {解|と}き{放|はな}って, etc. The passive form {解|と}き{放|はな}たれる is very common, especially in the figurative sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 〜から{解|と}き{放|はな}たれる: to be freed from ~
- {束縛|そくばく}から{解|と}き{放|はな}つ: to free from constraint
- {鳥|とり}を{解|と}き{放|はな}つ: to set a bird free
- {日常|にちじょう}から{解|と}き{放|はな}たれる: to be freed from daily life

SIMILAR WORDS:
{放|はな}す (to release, to let go) is simpler and more physical. {解放|かいほう}する (to liberate) is more formal and often used for political or social liberation. {解|と}き{放|はな}つ has a literary, dramatic quality and emphasizes the act of untying or unlocking before releasing.
